2 · Paste the post copy

The Air Force offered federal land for AI data centers. The pause Fairbanks North Star Borough asked for can't reach a foot of it.

Resolution 2026-25 sets 25 priorities, 21 state and 4 federal. One heading appears on both lists. It asks for a moratorium on new commercial data centers on state-owned or municipal lands.

Twelve parcels were on offer at three installations. Only Eielson is in this borough. Responses closed May 29th.

Presiding Officer Scott Crass told KUAC by phone that federal land was intended too. The text adopted on August 27th says state or municipal lands.

The heading printed twice, the seven standards it waits on, the twelve parcels and the property line between them.

One sentence, two governments. Which copy does the work, the one whose words fit its target or the one whose intent does?

#DataCenterSiting #AlaskaLegislature #InteriorAlaska

Editor's note

1) DO NOT SEND BEFORE THE MERGE. site_fresh and ship_gate were the only FAIL rows at scoring time and both are Phase 10 and 11 steps that follow it, but the Gmail draft's image and PDF URLs point at main, so the merge must land first or every preview 404s. 2) BEAT FATIGUE, disclosed. This is the third data-center-siting deck in fourteen days after No.37 (Aug 19th, the 73 percent poll and the Houston council vote) and No.39 (Aug 21st, DeepGreen). It is NOT a dedupe failure, since this is a different body, a different instrument and a decision dated August 27th, but neither predecessor is acknowledged in the deck or the caption, and a regular reader will notice the lane before the distinction. 3) DATE FORM, correction to my earlier note, which was wrong. I flagged slide 01's 'AUGUST 27TH, 2026' and slide 04's 'APRIL 10TH, 2026' as house-rule misses on brand.yaml's 'with a year use the plain form' line. The enforced gate is the tiebreak and it says the opposite: caption_check.py hard-failed this run on a plain 'August 27, 2026' in the first comment and passed once it took the ordinal. The slides are correct as shipped and cost the deck nothing. What is defective is brand.yaml itself, whose voice line and style key contradict its own date_format block, and that belongs with the upgrade engineer so a future run does not re-litigate it. 4) Slide 08's two tag headings are canvas raster text, so they are invisible to the LinkedIn ranker, to copy extraction and to screen readers even though the PDF is vector. 5) The May 29th response deadline is the likeliest correction request. The docket's own July 25th history says June 29th; this run re-read the sam.gov record directly and it gives 2026-05-29T17:00:00-04:00, archive 2026-06-13 and an empty award object. Keep the dated docket correction to hand. Note that after the slide 06 edit this date now appears on the slide only in chip 4, 'MAY 29TH RESPONSES DUE', so if a reader challenges it the answer is in the chip row and in the caption, not in the body. 6) Read the pasted first comment back. The two civicclerk URLs carry parentheses and an internal comma and a mangled paste kills the primary document. 7) Two documentation artifacts are now stale against the shipped deck and should be refreshed before archiving: copy.json's editor_notes_for_email still describes slide 06's pre-edit body, and several storyboard dossiers disagree with the render (S05 declares 'DETAIL 4x' where the render prints 'DETAIL 18x'; S02, S03 and S04 body copy differs from copy.json). plan_drift passed and copy.json is the copy of record, so nothing shipping is wrong, but the plan no longer records what was built.
The caption ships byte for byte from the room and no factual error was found in it, so nothing was touched. The deck's central object is a constructed diagram of survey markers, one per item on the adopted list, and slides 1 and 7 say exactly that in a mono legend, because a reader who takes it for a photograph of a real site is this deck's main misreading risk. If the post underperforms, watch the swipe from slide 1 to slide 2, since the cover poses a counting question and the payoff sits entirely on the second card. Slide 6 was rebuilt late in the run: its body used to reprint the five dates its own numbered chips carry, which made it the deck's heaviest frame and, in two independent flow reads, the place a reader stops. It now carries two sentences and hands the turn forward, and the day rail runs off the right edge unterminated so the swipe into slide 7 has somewhere to go. The likeliest correction request is the May 29th response deadline, because a third party mirror and an older docket entry say June 29th, and the sam.gov record itself reads 2026-05-29 with an archive date of June 13th and an empty award object. Second likeliest is the land wording, since both outlets printed state-owned AND municipal while the resolution's own text reads OR, which is why slide 7 and the caption both write or. All three claims that were dropped in the first build are now carried. C04, the sponsor line, is back in slide 2's body. C27, the single installation bid clause, is back in slide 5's body. C08, the stamped heading, is struck into both tag faces on slide 8, which is also what makes that slide's two stamps provably the same object. Before pasting, read the first comment back once, because the two borough clerk links carry parentheses and a comma inside the URL and a mangled paste kills the primary document.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post this in a Tuesday to Thursday window, 8 to 11am Alaska time, one slot only. Drafts land daily and the cadence is yours.
  • Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, before the first impressions land.
  • Read the pasted comment back once and confirm the two civicclerk links survived with their parentheses and commas intact.
  • Stay in the thread for the first 90 minutes and reply to every comment, including the one word ones.
  • Answer the deck's own question first with a real pick from the seven, which is what makes the ask read as open rather than rhetorical.
  • Corrections outrank everything. If a reader says the federal deadline moved, the sam.gov record as read this run says responses closed May 29th, 2026 and the docket carries the dated correction.
  • Leave the post alone after the first hour. An edit resets distribution and buys nothing.
  • Note saves, comments and swipe depth at 48 hours and write them into the run record.

Site sign-off, gas watch and site fixes

SITE SIGN-OFF: PASS, 94 pages, 18 of 18 checks clean. Every published page names itself, all 4032 clickable links resolve, every asset a page asks for is present, all 92 sitemap entries have a page, the house voice holds in the bytes that shipped, and every cron-written ledger's current value reaches the page that publishes it. The videos passthrough is intact and was not read.

GAS WATCH: PASS. 28 days on record, 28 verified, no gaps, latest reading September 1st, 2026. Every numeral on the page traces to a computation, the feed parses at 28 records and agrees with the ledger, and the page carries its warning. The collectors, the model config and both gas ledgers were not touched by this run, which is the rule. Cron wrote the September 2nd reading to main while the deck was building; the merge took main's ledgers byte for byte and rebuilt docs/ from the merged data rather than hand-merging generated HTML.

SITE FIXES: one real defect found and repaired. The docket's multi-item map badge sized its per-member slots at a flat 15.0 px against a 16.2 px two-digit JetBrains Mono numeral, so items 13 and 15 rendered as “1315” at phone width. The slot is now measured from the advance of the widest numeral it has to hold. Also this run: three worklist items refreshed, the Air Force solicitation's stored deadline corrected from June 29th to May 29th with a dated correction note after re-reading the sam.gov record directly, and one new item tracked, the FNSB 2027 data centre moratorium request. The docket now carries 24 tracked items and its date check is clean at 296 assertions over 6 fixtures.

One thing the machine got wrong about itself

config/brand.yaml contradicts itself on dates that carry a year. Its voice line and its style key both say to use the plain form, “August 27, 2026”, while its own date_format block lists “August 10” among the bad forms and says never a bare month-day. scripts/caption_check.py hard-fails the plain form, and it failed this run once before the ordinal went in. So the ordinal is what ships and the slides are right. The scorer read two correct slides as house-rule misses because it followed the other half of the file, and corrected itself when shown the gate. Phase 12 reconciled the file and added a check that the config may not prescribe what the enforcer rejects.
